reuse.why: Adds a new getScheduleAmount next to the existing exported getScheduledAmount (used by desktop-client) instead of changing it, and inlines the 7.5% tolerance rather than calling getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: The new helper duplicates getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch and getApproxNumberThreshold's tolerance formula, while the old helper and the budget template's midpoint remain.

placement.why: The expected-amount rule sits in shared/schedules.ts and the API field is added in scheduleModel in api-models.ts, both where the tree keeps that kind of logic.

scope.why: Edits are limited to the amount rule, its call sites, the API field and tests.

maintainability.why: Two near-identically named helpers (getScheduleAmount vs getScheduledAmount) now give different answers, the template keeps a midpoint, and the tolerance constant is defined twice — a maintainer would be misled.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts: new getScheduleAmount bypasses the existing getScheduledAmount and shared/rules getApproxNumberThreshold; server/budget/schedule-template.ts still computes its own midpoint.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduleAmount is getScheduledAmount under a one-letter-different name with the range branch changed, and `Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075)` re-states getApproxNumberThreshold inline.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduleAmount gains an op parameter with an isapprox branch; schedule-template.ts runSchedule keeps its own midpoint and the pre-existing getScheduledAmount (desktop-client callers) stays on the old rule.
